questions.text: In 2.200, what is the value of the digit 2 in the tenths place?
questions.solution: The tenths place is 1 place to the right of the decimal point. 2 tenths = 0.2.
questions.hint: Name each place as you move right from the decimal point.

questions.text: Round EACH number to the nearest whole number, then estimate the sum.
questions.solution: 2.38 rounds to 2 and 2.64 rounds to 3. Estimate: 2 + 3 = 5.
questions.hint: Look at the tenths digit to round each number first.

questions.text: Calculate the result.
questions.solution: Line up decimal points: 2.100 + 0.200 = 2.300. Add each column from right to left, regrouping 10 of one place as 1 of the next place.
questions.hint: Line up the decimal points. Add trailing zeros when needed.

questions.text: Your squad starts with 2.8 m of cable and uses 0.3 m to repair a Reboot Van prop. How many meters remain?
questions.solution: Line up decimal points: 2.800 − 0.300 = 2.500. Add zeros without changing the numbers. Regroup if a top digit is smaller. Check by adding back: 2.5 + 0.3 = 2.8.
questions.hint: Line up the decimal points. Add trailing zeros when needed.

questions.text: Calculate the result.
questions.solution: Line up decimal points: 2.780 + 1.670 = 4.450. Add each column from right to left, regrouping 10 of one place as 1 of the next place.
questions.hint: Line up the decimal points. Add trailing zeros when needed.

questions.text: Your squad starts with 2.32 m of cable and uses 1.78 m to repair a Reboot Van prop. How many meters remain?
questions.solution: Line up decimal points: 2.320 − 1.780 = 0.540. Add zeros without changing the numbers. Regroup if a top digit is smaller. Check by adding back: 0.54 + 1.78 = 2.32.
questions.hint: Line up the decimal points. Add trailing zeros when needed.

questions.text: Calculate the result.
questions.solution: Write 10 as 10.000. Regroup across the zeros: trade 1 whole for 10 tenths, 1 tenth for 10 hundredths, and 1 hundredth for 10 thousandths. Subtract in aligned columns: 10.000 − 3.875 = 6.125. Check: 3.875 + 6.125 = 10.
questions.hint: Write the whole number with three zeros after the decimal. Regroup one whole into 10 tenths, then continue trading to the right.

questions.text: Find the friendly pair. Add mentally.
questions.solution: 0.25 + 0.75 = 1. Add that whole to 2 to get 3.
questions.hint: The decimal parts together make one whole.

questions.text: At the training-island shop, a notebook costs $4.37. You pay $10.00. How much change should you get?
questions.solution: Subtract the cost from the amount paid: $10.00 − $4.37 = $5.63.
questions.hint: Change is the amount paid minus the cost.

questions.text: A player writes 2.2 + 0.47 = 0.69. They lined up the last digits instead of decimal points. What is the correct sum?
questions.solution: Line up the decimal points: 2.20 + 0.47 = 2.67. Last-digit alignment incorrectly treats tenths as hundredths.
questions.hint: Equivalent decimals and regrouping preserve value. Swapping digits does not.

questions.text: Calculate the result.
questions.solution: Line up decimal points: 2.200 + 1.340 = 3.540. Add each column from right to left, regrouping 10 of one place as 1 of the next place.
questions.hint: Line up the decimal points. Add trailing zeros when needed.

questions.text: Find the missing number. ___ + 1.24 = 2.875
questions.solution: Use the inverse relationship: 2.875 − 1.24 = 1.635. Check: 1.635 + 1.24 = 2.875.
questions.hint: Addition and subtraction undo each other.

questions.text: MATTER means…
questions.answer: Anything that has mass and takes up space
choices: Anything that has mass and takes up space
To use the senses to gain knowledge
The heaviness of an object
How hot or cold something is
questions.solution: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space: your squad training ball, the air inside it, even you!

questions.text: Fill in the equivalent decimal: 2.5 = ___ (write three decimal places).
questions.solution: 2.5 = 2.500. Trailing zeros do not change the value.
questions.hint: Zeros at the end of the decimal part do not change its value.

questions.text: Estimate 2.48 + 3.26 by rounding EACH number to a whole number. What should the sum be close to?
questions.solution: Round first: 2 + 3 = 5. An exact answer far from 5 needs another look.
questions.hint: An estimate is a check, not the exact answer.

question.text: Fill in the equivalent decimal: 2.5 = ___ (write three decimal places).
question.solution: 2.5 = 2.500. Trailing zeros do not change the value.
question.hint: Zeros at the end of the decimal part do not change its value.

questions.text: Calculate 1.2 × 2.
questions.solution: 1.2 × 2 = 2.4. Multiply 12 × 2 = 24; the factors have 1 decimal places in all. Divide that whole-number product by 10 and keep all places.
questions.hint: Think of equal groups. Multiply the digits and preserve the value of each decimal place.
questions.source: Provisional family-approved scope; 5.NBT.B.7. Chapter 4 contents unverified.

questions.text: Calculate 2.5 × 0.3.
questions.solution: 2.5 × 0.3 = 0.75. Multiply 25 × 03 = 75; the factors have 2 decimal places in all. Divide that whole-number product by 100 and keep all places.
questions.hint: Tenths times tenths give hundredths. Count places in both factors, then check the size.
questions.source: Provisional family-approved scope; 5.NBT.B.7. Chapter 4 contents unverified.

questions.text: A squad pours sand and steel paperclips into one supply tray. Why is this a mixture?
questions.answer: Two substances are combined and keep their original properties
choices: Two substances are combined and keep their original properties
The sand changes into steel
Every combination forms a new substance
The paperclips lose their magnetism
questions.solution: The sand is still sand, and the steel paperclips still have their own properties. Combining materials can make a mixture without a chemical change.
questions.hint: Ask whether the original materials keep their own properties.
